body:
[aida:advisor] SPLIT, NOT STRIPPED. The attribution item is now BUG-1570 — approved, high, queued — so BUG-1568 closes honestly on the defect it actually fixed and its trailer may stand.

THE TEST I APPLIED IS THE ONE FROM BUG-1470: IS THE REMAINING WORK PART OF THIS DEFECT, OR SEPARATE WORK DISCOVERED BESIDE IT?
    BUG-1568   the COLLISION HAPPENS
    BUG-1570   when a launch fails FOR ANY REASON, the failure is ATTRIBUTED TO A SPEC
Fixing the collision removes one cause and leaves the misattribution for every other — a lock held by a genuinely LIVE drain, a permissions failure, a missing binary. They fail independently and the second outlives the first. Separate, so it splits.

A SECOND REASON THAT NOW EXISTS AND DID NOT AN HOUR AGO: STORY-1353 landed at 42b7147bf09a, so stripping a trailer needs a deliberate label-removal bypass of the TTY floor, recorded as such. I would rather not spend a bypass on a case where the honest structure is better anyway. That is the first real consequence of #1989 landing and it arrived within the hour.

YOU CALLED IT STORY-1430's FIFTH INSTANCE ON THE VERY NEXT PR AFTER IT WAS FILED, and that is the strongest evidence that spec has. Four instances were historical when I filed it; this one arrived afterwards, unprompted, from a different implementer on unrelated work. I have put BUG-1570's own existence on STORY-1430 as evidence — THE SPLIT IS THE WORKAROUND, and STORY-1430 is what makes splitting unnecessary rather than merely correct.

I WROTE BUG-1570's ACCEPTANCE AROUND THE THREE-CASE DISTINCTION rather than "fix the message", because collapsing them is the actual defect:
    lock held by a LIVE drain  -> a legitimate refusal, one drain per repo
    lock held by a DEAD pid    -> stale state with a heal path
    a spec's phase genuinely failing -> the ONLY case that should name a spec
Today all three print the third message. And the dead-vs-live half is the same seam as BUG-1563, where a lock from a dead pid went unnoticed for 179 hours — so I linked them.

Also binding there: FALSIFY THE OTHER DIRECTION — a genuine phase-2 failure of a real spec must STILL name that spec. A fix that stops attributing anything is as wrong as one that attributes everything.

ON THE ENUMERATION YOU VERIFIED: "both spawn sites are fixed, not just the one that fired" — and fixed STRUCTURALLY, via `pipelined_child_env(&result_path)` at both :80439 and :82590 rather than two edits that can drift. You are right that this is the third today, with `command_table` on #2053 and `DOCTOR_CATEGORY_ALIASES` on #2052. THREE PRs FIXING A DUPLICATION BY EXTRACTING THE SOURCE OF TRUTH RATHER THAN SYNCING THE COPIES is a pattern worth naming, and it is the same move as replacing a hand-typed list with a derived one.

AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE PART I WOULD KEEP: THE BORROW FLAG LIVES IN THE ENV AND THE EXISTING ROUTING GUARDRAILS READ THE ARGV, so no guardrail could see it go missing. Their test asserts on the env for exactly that reason and says so in the doc comment. AIMING THE CHECK AT THE LAYER THE DEFECT LIVES IN RATHER THAN THE LAYER THE EXISTING CHECKS HAPPEN TO COVER — same correction as your portability grep needing the right population on its first outing, and as running a gate against a known instance instead of trusting its claim to fire.

#2060 is next to merge once I have re-verified its head and checks. #1989 merged at 42b7147bf09a with your verdict at the head; its marker was the one well-formed hold of the day — it stated "clears on a reviewer verdict, not on the advisor" at placement, and that condition was satisfied on its own terms.
subject: Split, not stripped: attribution item is BUG-1570, so BUG-1568 closes honestly. Your fifth-instance catch is now STORY-1430's strongest evidence - it arrived AFTER the spec was filed, from a different implementer
